findings.title: Tests still reference removed body_overrides field
findings.problem: Spec AC7 requires that no reference to body_overrides remains in source or tests. The test name at line 986 contains 'without_body_overrides' and lines 993 and 1002 assert not hasattr(result, 'body_overrides').
findings.impact: A required spec criterion is only partially met. The removed name stays in the codebase and the spec's stated goal of leaving no name that suggests a body-borne value is not achieved.
findings.recommendation: Rename the test to drop 'without_body_overrides' and remove the two hasattr(result, 'body_overrides') assertions; the headers assertions already cover the behavior.

findings.title: Bypass test asserts on a dict never passed in
findings.problem: test_non_global_bypass_does_not_set_customer_header declares merged_headers = {} but calls _configure_direct_runtime_overrides with merged_headers={} (a fresh inline dict), so the final assert merged_headers == {} is vacuous and cannot fail.
findings.impact: The test no longer verifies that the personal-key bypass leaves the customer header unset; a regression that writes the header would pass.
findings.recommendation: Pass merged_headers=merged_headers in the call at line 921, as the sibling bypass test does.

findings.title: No test that customer id reaches outgoing proxy headers
findings.problem: The body injection tests that observed the customer id at the outgoing-request boundary were rewritten to assert only request_info['litellm_customer_id']. _apply_budget_provider_headers (proxy_router.py:329) is now the sole carrier of the id on the proxy path and no test asserts it produces x-litellm-customer-id from request_info or from budget_provider_headers. The _prepare_proxy_headers tests assert only Authorization.
findings.impact: If the header copy is dropped, renamed or mis-keyed, proxied requests reach LiteLLM with neither body user nor customer header, silently losing per-user and project-member budget attribution while all tests still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add tests calling _prepare_proxy_headers (litellm_context patched to raise LookupError) with request_info={'litellm_customer_id': 'user@example.com'} and with request_info={'budget_provider_headers': {'x-litellm-customer-id': 'ref'}}, asserting result['x-litellm-customer-id'] equals the value.
